info.name: Sally-K API — Checkout (Cart, Orders, Payments)
info.description: One consistent example story runs through this collection: buyer 'Order Test Buyer' adds 2x 'Order Test Sneaker' (₦15,000 each) to their cart from seller 'Order Test Store', pays via Paystack, and the seller marks the resulting order fulfilled. All sample IDs/values below are taken from real responses during backend testing — shapes are accurate, specific IDs will differ per request.

request.description: Required `size`/`color` only if the product defines those options; must be one of the product's own values. Adding the same product+size+color again merges quantity into the existing line instead of duplicating it.

response.name: 201 Created
400 Bad Request — missing required size
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "Select a size for this product" }

response.name: 200 OK
200 OK

request.description: Public, no auth. Use this to get the Paystack publishable key instead of hardcoding it in the frontend.

No request body — prices and validates whatever is currently in the buyer's cart (same stock/active checks as cart add). Does NOT create any Order yet and does NOT touch stock/cart — that only happens once payment is verified as successful.

Use `accessCode` to open Paystack's Inline.js popup (recommended — card + bank transfer channels, card data never touches our backend), or redirect the browser to `authorizationUrl` for the hosted checkout page. Both show the same two channels since the backend restricts `channels: ["card", "bank_transfer"]`.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — product no longer available
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "\"Order Test Sneaker\" is no longer available" }

request.description:
Call this right after Paystack redirects back / the Inline popup resolves, passing the same `reference` from Initialize. This is what actually confirms payment with Paystack server-to-server AND creates the Order(s) — one per seller in the cart — decrements stock, and clears the cart.

Idempotent: calling it again for an already-paid reference just returns the same orders again, it will not double-charge or double-create.

header.value: <computed by Paystack, HMAC-SHA512 of the raw body with your secret key>

request.description: Not something the frontend ever calls — Paystack calls this server-to-server when configured in the Paystack dashboard. Requires a public URL (e.g. ngrok) to reach localhost, so in local dev the Verify endpoint above is the one that actually drives the flow. Included here only so the shape is documented. Signature is verified against the raw request bytes; an invalid/missing signature gets 401.
